title: Rolo and the Spooky Shed
markdown:
Rolo and Marmalade loved helping Grandma Bear. Oh, Grandma Bear! She made the most splendid jams in the whole wide forest. Blackberry, raspberry, strawberry – you name it, she jarred it. And this particular afternoon, the air was thick with the sweet scent of warm blackberries. Grandma Bear hummed a happy tune as she stirred the bubbling jam in her biggest, shiniest pot. It was the last batch of the season, and Rolo’s tummy rumbled just thinking about it.

“Almost there, my dears!” she chirped, her apron dusted with flour. Her spectacles perched on the end of her nose as she peered into the pot. “Just the very last potful to jar up. Oh, but… oh dearie me!” Grandma Bear frowned, patting her apron pockets, then her little apron drawers. “I seem to be missing the lid for this last, most perfect jar of blackberry jam! The *very* last one!”

Rolo’s bushy tail gave a little twitch. He loved Grandma Bear’s jam. He *really* loved it. And he knew, with a little shiver that went all the way down to his furry toes, where the spare lids were kept. In the shed. The shed at the edge of the garden. The shed that was a bit dark. A bit dusty. And – oh dear – a bit spooky. This was Rolo’s secret worry: dark, dusty, and quiet places made him feel wobbly-kneed. He was afraid of the unknown, of what his imagination could conjure in shadows.

“Don’t you worry, Grandma Bear!” Rolo said, trying to sound much braver than he felt. He puffed out his chest, making himself look as tall as possible. “Marmalade and I will go and find the lid! We will!” He squeezed Marmalade, who was tucked under his arm, for extra courage. Marmalade’s soft fur was always so comforting.

“We must hurry!” Grandma Bear said cheerfully, though a little worriedly. “This jam will be just perfect, but it needs its lid *right* away, or it might get… well, too cool!” A cool lid, she implied, was a sad lid indeed. And Rolo knew, with a feeling like a tiny grey cloud settling in his chest, that if he didn't go now, he might miss out on the very best jam. If he didn’t go now, the jam might not be perfect for the picnic tomorrow! He really, really wanted that jam!

“Come on, Marmalade!” Rolo whispered, taking a deep, shaky breath. He scooped up his plush friend and tiptoed towards the garden gate. The shed loomed ahead, its wooden door slightly ajar, looking like a sleepy yawn in the afternoon sun. *It’s just a door,* Rolo told himself firmly, trying to ignore the way his whiskers twitched. *A perfectly normal door. Not a yawning mouth. Nope!*

Taking another deep breath that smelled of grass and flowers, Rolo pushed the shed door open. WHOOOOSH went the hinges, a little louder than he expected. It sounded like the shed was grumbling hello. Inside, it wasn't exactly *pitch* black, but the sunlight struggled to get through the dusty windowpanes, casting long, wavy shadows on the floor. There were piles of forgotten flowerpots, a very old rake that looked like a giant metal spider with too many legs, and… shadows. Lots of shadows that seemed to dance when he moved.

Rolo’s heart started to go thump-thump-thumpety-thump against his ribs. He clutched Marmalade so tightly his plush friend felt like a fuzzy little rock. “Okay, Marmalade,” he whispered, his voice a little squeaky, like a mouse trying to roar. “We’re looking for a lid. A round, shiny lid. It’s for the jam.” He tried to focus, to ignore the strange shapes in the corners, but then a shadow seemed to stretch and move in the dim light. Was it… a giant, shadowy creature? His whiskers quivered, and he felt a strong urge to turn tail and scamper back to Grandma Bear’s warm kitchen, jam or no jam. He almost froze, his paws glued to the dusty floor. But then, he felt Marmalade’s soft, familiar fur against his cheek. Marmalade, who was always brave with him, who never made him feel silly for being scared.

“Okay, Rolo,” he whispered to himself, his voice a little steadier now. “Marmalade is here. We can do this. We just need that lid.” He shuffled his paws, trying to remember why he was here. Oh yes! The lid! He squinted, his eyes darting over dusty jars and old watering cans. And then he saw it! High up on a shelf, tucked away behind a stack of old, dented buckets, glinting faintly in a sliver of light, was a perfect, round jar lid!

“There it is!” Rolo chirped, a little louder this time, a wave of relief washing over him. But oh! It was so high. So, *so* high. Tucked behind a lopsided stack of old, dented buckets that looked like they might tumble with just a gentle breeze. Rolo’s breath hitched. He’d have to climb. Climb the wobbly buckets. His paws felt suddenly slippery, and he imagined himself tumbling down, down, down, with a loud clatter. He clutched Marmalade tight. "Okay, Marmalade," he whispered, "you stay right here. I have to go get the lid. Don't worry, I'll be right back." Leaving his best friend, even for a moment, felt like a heavy stone in his tummy. As he stepped onto the lowest bucket, it wobbled precariously. A gust of wind rustled through the shed, making the buckets sway like a boat on a stormy sea. He felt a definite tremor under his paws – a vibration that went right up his legs and made his knees feel like jelly. He could almost hear the CLANG of buckets hitting the floor and feel the dust flying up into his face. But Rolo kept climbing, his claws finding tiny grips, his eyes fixed on the prize. Slowly, carefully, he reached the top. With a triumphant little squeak, he grabbed the lid, but for a brief, terrifying moment, the space where Marmalade had been felt cold and empty.

Victory! He carefully climbed back down, feeling a little shaky but immensely proud. He scooped up Marmalade, who gave a little plush purr, and together, they scampered back out into the bright sunshine, the precious lid held carefully in Rolo’s paws. Oh, the sunshine felt so good!

Grandma Bear gasped with delight. “My goodness, Rolo! You found it! You are such a brave, clever boy!” She took the lid and, with a satisfying pop, sealed the last jar of blackberry jam. The kitchen filled with the most wonderful, sweet, fruity aroma, a smell that promised warmth and happiness.

Rolo watched, his heart swelling with a happy, buzzy feeling. He looked back towards the shed, and it didn’t seem so scary anymore. It was just a shed. A place with old things. And he, Rolo the raccoon, had been brave enough to go in and get what was needed. He felt a new kind of warmth spreading through him, even better than the promise of jam.

Later, when a particularly shadowy corner of the den made its usual attempt to look like a grumpy badger, Rolo didn't feel his whiskers droop or his paws get clammy. Instead, he took a deep breath, and the smell of dusty wood from the shed filled his nose. He remembered the feel of the wobbly buckets under his paws, the slight tremor that ran through him, and the triumphant, light feeling of reaching the top. He just winked at the shadow, knowing it was only a shadow, and went to find a cookie.
characters: Rolo the raccoon, Marmalade the marmalade cat plush
